label: Escalating Ladder
line: Name a measure and both ends, then climb: each step is a label, a number and a picture the viewer knows, joined to the last by a comparison, with the strangest step last.
best_for: something with a natural measure: size, cost, speed, time to break, risk, depth
a 'what would happen if' question with a real constant
options ranked from worst to best by one test
also_for: a list of items, when one measure can order them
avoid_for: steps that are only bigger numbers with nothing to compare them to
a measure so subjective the steps could be reordered
signals: one measure orders everything in it
each step can be compared with something the viewer knows
the last step is far beyond the first
the steps could not be reordered

beats.name: Frame
beats.job: The measure and both ends, or the bottom step tied to something in the viewer's world.

beats.name: Steps 1 to 3
beats.job: One step at a time: a label, one number, one picture. Each transition compares it with the step before.

beats.name: Leave the frame
beats.job: Go past where the viewer thought it ended, or speak their objection. For a what-if: the law that should stop it, then set it aside.

beats.name: Top step
beats.job: The thing the title named, or the most extreme case.

beats.name: Twist or stop
beats.job: Stop on the number, or redefine what 'top' means.

hooks.shape: From [the cheap end] all the way to [the expensive end]. The test: [one thing you can measure].
In [year], [the old thing] held [a small amount], about [one familiar object].
Here is what would happen if you [premise].
How many [X] can you [lose] and still [function]? Start with the easy ones.

holds: Escalation is the engine: every transition is a comparison with the step before. A running score is a progress bar. The strongest re-opening comes where the ladder leaves the frame the viewer expected. A long what-if ladder earns its length only by re-opening the question every few steps.
ending: The top step's number, or a twist on what the top is. Stop there.
first_frame: Both ends of the scale, or the bottom step with its anchor object and the empty ladder above it.
pitfalls: The surprise spent in the first sentence
Numbers with nothing to compare them to
template: [The measure] runs from [bottom] to [top]. Bottom: [item 1], [number], about [a picture the viewer knows]. Next: [item 2], [comparison], [number], [a bigger picture]. Next: [item 3]. You might think that is the top. [The step beyond]. Top: [the title's item], [its most vivid number]. The real top: [twist].
